summary: 1943 tower on Bearden Knob, Tucker County, built to replace the Canaan Mountain cabin; sources list it as removed; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: built entirely of wood timbers (NHLR history)
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts page marks it Removed; firelookout.org index lists it as Tower Gone

events.note: Erected on the Cheat Ranger District to replace the obsolete Canaan Mountain lookout

evidence.supports: Bearden Knob tower erected in 1943 on the Cheat Ranger District
evidence.quote: Bearden Knob Tower, on the Cheat Ranger District, was erected in 1943

evidence.supports: tower built in 1943 as a replacement for the obsolete Canaan Mountain tower
evidence.quote: This tower was built in 1943 as a replacement for the obsolete Canaan Mountain Fire Tower.

evidence.supports: Canaan Mountain lookout was a wood-framed cabin built atop a large rock in 1924
evidence.quote: Constructed in 1924, the Canaan Mountain Lookout was not a steel tower but a wood-framed, live-in cabin with a wraparound porch, built atop a large rock.

evidence.supports: Canaan cabin abandoned in 1943 for the new Bearden Knob tower, two miles away
evidence.quote: abandoned in 1943 in favor of the newly built Bearden Knob Lookout Tower, located two miles away.

evidence.supports: Army training context: Forest added towers in the northern half of the forest
evidence.quote: To increase wildfire protection in the northern half of the Forest while the U.S. Army trained soldiers in the West Virginia Maneuver Area (WVMA)

evidence.supports: four additional towers erected in 1943 and 1944
Army funded three temporary lookout towers around 1943, Bearden Knob among them
evidence.quote: c.1943: Army funding was used to construct three temporary lookout towers for fire protection, one of which was the Bearden Knob tower on the Chert Ranger District near Davis.

evidence.supports: Bearden Knob built entirely of wood timbers, as were a few other towers
evidence.quote: a few, like Bearden Knob, Niges Cliff, Pigeons Roost towers, were constructed entirely of wood timbers.

evidence.supports: firelookout.org index lists Bearden Knob as Tower Gone
evidence.quote: Bearden Knob Tucker 39.10531 -79.42607 Tower Gone FFLOS US 152, WV 2

evidence.supports: site registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites register in September 2008
most Forest towers were razed, leaving concrete piers and steps
evidence.quote: Most, however, were simply razed, leaving only their concrete piers and steps as the evidence of their existence.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts names the Chert Ranger District; the NHLR Monongahela history names the Cheat Ranger District. The story follows the NHLR history.
Forest Lookouts calls the 1943 towers temporary; the NHLR history describes Bearden Knob as built entirely of wood timbers and does not call it temporary. Both are reported as stated.

sources.title: Fire Towers: Fifty Years of Early Detection and Fire Protection
Walking the Old Watch: Former Fire Tower Hikes in the Monongahela

notes_for_editor: Built year (1943) is supported by two sources. Removal is stated only as Removed (Forest Lookouts) and Tower Gone (index); no removal date found. No staffing history found for Bearden Knob. Access and present condition of the site are unknown; no photos added. Canaan Mountain cabin is a separate site (dismantled 1946) and is mentioned only as background. Brief record matched on name, county, coordinates, agency and 2008 registration; no corrections proposed.
